name: What's the difference between a traditional tank water heater and a tankless water heater when hot water runs out fast?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a traditional tank water heater and a tankless water heater when hot water runs out fast?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional tank water heater stores a finite amount of hot water, which, once depleted, requires time to reheat. If your hot water runs out fast, it means you've used up the stored supply. A tankless water heater, however, heats water on demand as it flows through the unit, providing a continuous supply of hot water. This means a tankless system generally won't 'run out' of hot water in the same way a tank system does, making it an excellent option for homes with high hot water demand.
acceptedAnswer.description: Traditional tanks store limited hot water, which can run out, while tankless heaters provide a continuous, on-demand supply.
